shared_elements: tall standing monolithic pillar/figure carved in low relief
circular disc set on the body
sinuous serpent-like or curved linear motifs
paired symmetrical motifs across the upper zone
schematic anthropomorphising of the block (head/shoulder zone above, body below)
justification: Both surfaces treat a tall block as a schematic body carrying shallow relief organised in stacked zones, with a prominent circular disc on the torso, a horizontal band or belt below it, sinuous serpentine lines, and paired symmetrical motifs across the upper register. But A's content is dominated by clearly readable animals in profile (quadrupeds, a long-necked bird, a snake) and small human-like figures with a fringed band, whereas B's carving is almost entirely abstract curvilinear and mask-like forms with no identifiable animals, so the shared traits are largely generic monolith-decoration conventions rather than a common specific scheme.
